newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia denies report of spy defecting to West.
newsitem.headline: Russia denies report of spy defecting to West.

text.p: Russia on Monday denied a German magazine report that a Russian secret service agent had defected with the names of hundreds of Russian spies operating in Germany.

"It's absolute nonsense," said Tatyana Samolis, spokeswoman for the Foreign Intelligence Service. "To speak of hundreds of people, that just doesn't happen. Any defector could get the name of one, two, perhaps three agents, not hundreds."

Samolis was responding to a report in the German magazine Focus, which quoted reliable sources as saying a renegade Russian intelligence office had given extensive material from the KGB record office to the British secret service.
The information with references to hundreds of Russian spies supposedly working in German government circles was turned over to Bonn earlier this year, said the report published this week.
"Do you think that the KGB has some kind of box or a computer that you can just push a button and get an entire list of agents? It just doesn't happen," Samolis said.
"We don't have any information that anyone has defected in the last few weeks or months," she added.
Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service is the international arm of the former KGB secret service.
